- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days — adjust for a gradual downward bias correction after initial spike.
- When true values show sharp upward momentum (e.g., >70 → >80), model tends to overshoot and then correct — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to observed spike.
- Model underestimates when true values are near or below 70, especially after a recent dip — increase forecast slightly to avoid “mean reversion trap”.
- Forecast tends to lag true values by 1–3 days in the middle of the horizon — shift forecast forward by 1–2 days for mid-range predictions.
- When history shows a recent sharp decline (e.g., 65–67), model often fails to anticipate rebound — increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to capture rebound momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values — if last 5 days are above 75, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days to prevent “overheating” bias.
